description: Equipo basado en San Luis Potosí formado por alumnos de la UASLP
summary: This project consists of a series of interfaces that display information of the body of an astronaut in a space mission, such as sleep schedule, heart, bone mass, radiation on the body, muscular mass, and metabolism are displayed clearly, and with visual guides to make it more intuitive. The system detects any anomaly and appoints activities to prevent any possible future health risks, as well as recreational activities to deal with mental problems, caused by stress, isolation, and other factors. This system gives the astronaut more autonomy to make decisions when communications with earth have very long latency, or become impractical, as it happens the further your mission gets further away from earth.
details:
Our system presents essential medical data required to monitor and determine health conditions based on physical status and environmental factors in accordance with the mission. The acquired data is broken down comprehensively, categorized by body regions, as well as mandatory and recreational activities aimed at ensuring overall well-being. These records can be reviewed through regional statistical breakdowns and an interactive body visualization.

The projected scope for implementation focuses on continuous, all-condition health monitoring for astronauts, evaluating the risks and variables they face, and determining proper courses of action. Because specific mission destinations may occasionally prevent immediate communication or response from Earth, personnel must be equipped to act autonomously.

Tools and Programming Languages:

>XAMPP and DBeaver (for our database): Implementation and management.

>PHP, CSS, HTML

>Figma

>Canva

Utilized to enhance visual appeal and intuitive design, prioritizing the comfort of the user (in this case, the astronaut) rather than administrative personnel. Furthermore, this system is designed to accompany and "aid" the astronaut rather than merely monitor and display information. We provide both the data and actionable guidance based on the results shown, aiming to mitigate risks and ensure a safer journey with enhanced physical and mental health.
